content:
Miley Cyrus paid tribute to her late godmother Dolly Parton this week upon receiving news that they’d received a shared Grammy Award nomination.

Parton, who died Aug. 25 at age 80, and Cyrus are nominated for Best Country Duo/Group Performance for their rendition of Parton’s 1977 hit, “Light of a Clear Blue Morning,” which also features vocals by Queen Latifah, Reba McEntire and Lainey Wilson.

In an emotional post shared to Instagram and X Monday, Cyrus called the nomination a “beautiful way to honor [Parton’s] enormous heart,” noting that proceeds from the song supported pediatric cancer research at Vanderbilt’s Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital in Nashville, Tennessee.

“My Aunt Dolly is one of the greatest songwriters the world has ever known,” Cyrus wrote. “She never made music for recognition but to make the world a happier place through her songs.”

“I miss her calling on big days like this but feel her in every moment. Love you Aunt Dolly,” she continued. “Congratulations to these beautiful women and all the other nominees.”

In addition to the Grammy nod for “Light of a Clear Blue Morning,” Parton received a second nomination in the Best Country Duo/Group Performance category for “Butterfly,” performed with the Zac Brown Band. She’s also nominated for Best Audio Book, Narration, and Storytelling Recording for the audio edition of her 2025 memoir, “Star of the Show: My Life on Stage.”

Fellow nominees in the Best Country Duo/Group Performance include
Kacey Musgraves and Miranda Lambert for “Horses and Divorces,” Lainey Wilson and John Mayer for “Phone, Keys, Wallet,” and Mumford & Sons and Chris Stapleton for “Here.”

Cyrus and Parton collaborated on a host of musical projects over the years, including “Rainbowland,” a track off of Cyrus’ 2017 album, “Younger Now,” and “Christmas Is,” which appeared on Parton’s 2020 holiday album, “A Holly Dolly Christmas.”

In 2022, the two women co-hosted “Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party” on NBC, performing spirited renditions of their songs “Wrecking Ball” and “I Will Always Love You” in duet.

An 11-time Grammy winner, Parton died Aug. 25 after a brief battle with cancer at a Tennessee hospital.

Speaking to People in an interview conducted four days before her death, the country legend acknowledged she’d been grappling with “some health issues that I just didn’t pay attention to” prior to the 2025 death of her husband, Carl Dean.

Still, she reassured fans that she intended to forge ahead with a series of creative projects, including “Dolly: A True Original Musical,” which is slated to open on Broadway in January 2027.
